screen_type.instructions: The image is a screenshot of one screen of a web app; numbered boxes mark its interactive elements. What kind of screen is it?

criteria.landing: start or welcome page that routes the user elsewhere
criteria.list: a collection of items: rows, cards or a table
criteria.form: fields to create or edit something
criteria.dashboard: overview of several summaries, counts or recent items
criteria.dialog: a modal, drawer or popup menu over another screen
criteria.empty: a screen with no content yet
criteria.error: an error, not-found or access-denied message

primary_action.instructions: Look at the screenshot as a first-time user. Is there one main action this screen invites?

criteria.one-clear: one action stands out by position, size or colour

hierarchy.instructions: How clear is the visual hierarchy of this screen: does the eye know where to look first and what belongs together?

title_matches.instructions: Does the screen's heading name the object or the task this screen is about?

criteria.true: the heading names what the screen shows or lets the user do
criteria.false: no heading, a generic heading (app name, 'Home') or one that does not match the content

location.instructions: Does the screen show where the user is: an active navigation item, a breadcrumb or a selected tab?

criteria.true: a highlighted nav item, breadcrumb or selected tab marks the current place
criteria.false: nothing on the screen shows the current place in the app

density.instructions: How dense is the content of this screen?

criteria.crowded: many elements compete for space and attention

labels.instructions: Are the labels of buttons, links and headings in words a first-time user understands?

criteria.plain-words: everyday words that say what happens
criteria.some-jargon: a few internal, technical or abbreviated terms
criteria.jargon-or-icon-only: mostly jargon, or many controls carry only an icon

icon_only.instructions: Are important actions shown only as icons, without a text label or tooltip?

criteria.true: at least one important action is an unlabelled icon

scent.instructions: The image shows the start screen of a web app; numbered boxes mark its interactive elements and the state lists them. The state names a persona and a task. Which numbered element would this persona click first to get the task done?
scent.path_instructions: The image shows one screen of a web app; numbered boxes mark its interactive elements. The state names a persona, a task, the step of the task and what the persona clicked to get here. The persona scans this screen in reading order, a few elements at a time: the state lists only the current group, each as 'letter = mark number: role "label"'; ignore every other numbered box. Which letter would this persona click now to get on with the task? Answer next when none of the listed elements looks right and the persona would read on; when more_marks_after_this is false, next means the persona would click nothing on this screen.

synonyms.instructions: The state names two labels a web app shows on different screens, with the screens they appear on. True only when both are names for the same kind of thing, one object type under two names (e.g. 'Invite' and 'Invitation'). False when one is a part, setting, link or list of the other, or the name of one particular item (e.g. 'Organization settings' for 'Organization', 'Acme / Main' for 'Workspace').

match.instructions: A first-time user of a web app clicked the control named in the state (`clicked`, on screen `from`) and said beforehand what it would show (`predicted`: kind of screen, heading, object, purpose). `observed` and the image show what it actually showed. True when the prediction got the gist right: the same object or purpose, a similar kind of screen; other wording is fine. False when this user would be surprised: another object or purpose, or a menu or dialog where a page with content was expected (or the other way round).

criteria.true: the user finds what they expected
criteria.false: the user is surprised by what appears

walk_match.instructions: A user of a web app performed the step in the state and wrote beforehand what they expected (`expected`) and afterwards what happened (`outcome`). True when the outcome is what they expected, false when it surprised them or nothing happened.

rules.text: No clear visual hierarchy: the eye finds no focal point.
Several actions compete for attention; none reads as the main one.
No main action is visible on a screen that should invite one.

label.en: Heading does not name the screen

rules.text: The heading does not name what this screen shows or does.
Nothing shows where the user is: no active nav item, breadcrumb or selected tab.
The screen is crowded: many elements compete for space and attention.
Some labels use internal or technical terms.
Labels are mostly jargon or icons only.
Important actions are icons without a text label or tooltip.
The predicted first look misses the primary action:
Content overflows its container and is cut off or scrolls sideways.
Interactive elements overlap each other.
Click targets are smaller than 24×24 px (WCAG 2.5.8).
One object goes by several names (OOUX P13).
A first-time user expected something else from this click.
The control looked like it would do one thing and did another.
Something turned up where a first-time user did not expect it.
The app's names mislead: one thing under two names, or one name for two things.
The task's target screen is more than 4 clicks from the start.
The persona could not finish the task.
rules.rate_text: Half or more of the personas could not finish the task.

rules.text: The persona finished the task but struggled.
rules.rate_text: At least half of the personas failed the task or finished it only with detours.

label.en: Hard step in a task walk

rules.text: The persona rated this step hard (SEQ 1-7) or much harder than the step before.
First click goes astray: the persona would start somewhere else than the path to the task.
rules.path_text: Click goes astray: the persona would leave the path to the task here.

label.en: Wrong click before the right one

rules.text: Click taken too early: scanning in reading order, the persona picks a wrong element before reaching the one on the path.
A write request reached the server during a readonly run.

seq.question: Overall, how difficult or easy was this step? 1 = very difficult, 7 = very easy.
sus_items: I think that I would like to use this system frequently.
I found the system unnecessarily complex.
I thought the system was easy to use.
I think that I would need the support of a technical person to be able to use this system.
I found the various functions in this system were well integrated.
I thought there was too much inconsistency in this system.
I would imagine that most people would learn to use this system very quickly.
I found the system very cumbersome to use.
I felt very confident using the system.
I needed to learn a lot of things before I could get going with this system.

sus_suspect.text: SUS answers by pattern: the odd items share one answer and the even items share one (all equal, or alternating perfectly). Such a walk is flagged sus_suspect and left out of every SUS mean.

personas.variant_text: A variant is the same role played by a different person: vary digital literacy (low: unsure with web apps, reads every label, avoids icons; high: scans, tries shortcuts), hurry (true: skims and clicks the first plausible thing) and prior domain knowledge (none: does not know the field's words; expert: expects its usual terms and places). Spread the variants: no two alike, at least one with low literacy or no domain knowledge.
